Qwen/Qwen3-32B.answer: Your symptoms suggest postural imbalances and mobility restrictions affecting the chest, shoulders, hips, and feet. The pectoral/trapezius pain during cross-body movement may relate to scapular dyskinesis or ribcage tightness. Limited leg rotations and knee clicking could stem from hip mobility issues. Plantar pain likely involves foot mechanics or compensatory pronation.
recommended_exercises: Hip-Dip Stretch for QL Lengthening and Rib Cage Expansion
Seated Scapular Separation with Rib Cage Expansion
Standing Wall Press for Upright Posture Progression
key_points: A stretch designed to lengthen the Quadratus Lumborum (QL) muscle and promote rib cage expansion on the compressed side, performed with one elbow on an elevated surface.

This exercise aims to improve the resting position of the shoulder blades on the rib cage and enhance the capacity for posterior rib cage expansion during breathing. It addresses upper back muscle knots by promoting better muscle length and reducing tension through controlled movement and breathwork.

Scapular winging is often associated with a rounded forward shoulder and compression/tightness in the front of the ribcage. Addressing the ability of the ribcage to open and expand, particularly during breathing, is vital. Without proper ribcage mobility and breathing mechanics, strengthening muscles to reposition the scapula may not lead to lasting changes, as the body won't know how to maintain the open space.

This exercise is a progression from the supine version, designed to transfer the learned pelvic alignment and center of gravity shift into an upright, standing posture. It focuses on maintaining proper foot and pelvic contact points against a wall while breathing.
cautions: Do not arch the back/rib cage up, as this will engage the QL more and the abs less.
Avoid going too low and chasing sensation, which can lead to compensatory movements like shoulder hiking.
Shrugging the shoulders or depressing the chest.
Applying too much force (more than 1-2/10 effort) when separating hands, as this can build tension in the shoulders.

Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507.answer: El dolor en el pectoral y trapecio superior derecho al tocar el ombligo contrario, junto con la rotación interna limitada en la pierna izquierda y externa en la derecha, y el sonido en la rodilla derecha durante sentadillas, sugiere una asimetría postural y restricciones en la movilidad del tórax y las caderas. El dolor en la planta del pie derecho al caminar indica posible desalineación en el contacto del pie, especialmente en la función del arco plantar y la pronación compensatoria.
